methodological_rigor.justification: The study analyzes 321 neuroblastic tumors (255 NB, 48 GNB, 18 GN) prospectively collected through a national cooperative group (JCCG-JNBSG) using a triangulated set of molecular assays: C-circle qPCR with validated cut-offs, TERT mRNA qPCR, TERT break-apart FISH, TERT promoter Sanger sequencing, ATRX genomic qPCR/CGH+SNP array/Sanger sequencing, and 60K array CGH. Assays are performed in triplicate and calibrated against the ALT+ cell line SK-N-FI; cut-offs are pre-specified from prior literature. Central pathological review and central molecular diagnostics add methodological strength. Minor limitations include small subgroup sizes (especially GN, n=18), absence of outcome/survival data to connect TMM status to prognosis in the GNB/GN arms, and the authors explicitly acknowledge this.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work provides the first systematic, standardized assessment of TMM in a sizable GNB cohort and links TMM activation to nodular GNB histology and to ATRX alterations, offering direct implications for refinement of the INRG risk classification and potential stratification for telomerase/ALT-targeted therapies (BET inhibitors, ATM/PARP inhibitors). Translational relevance is concrete and actionable even without outcome data. Classified as Oxford LoE 4 as an observational biomarker/case-series study without prospective outcomes analysis or a control comparison.

reporting_quality.justification: As a biomarker study, REMARK applies; most items (patient cohort definition, assay methods with manufacturer details, cut-off derivation, statistical analysis) are well reported, as are tables of clinical characteristics and stratification. Supplementary tables (SI, SII) cover primer sequences and clinical information. Gaps include absence of a CONSORT-style flow diagram, no explicit pre-registration, limited reporting of assay performance characteristics (e.g., reproducibility CVs), and no data/code availability statement identifiable in the main text — CGH data and raw qPCR values do not appear to be deposited in a repository.

novelty_literature.justification: TMM activation in neuroblastoma is established, but systematic analysis of TMM across a large GNB cohort (n=48) with a single standardized C-circle assay is genuinely novel, as acknowledged against a prior meta-analysis of only 12 GNB cases. Identification of a 12.5 Mb recurrent 7q gain region in ALT(+) NTs and demonstration that all six ALT(+) GNBs harbored ATRX alterations are new findings relevant for future INRG revision. The TERT activation mechanism in GNB (mostly without rearrangement/promoter mutation) is an interesting open mechanism flagged for future work.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with logical structure (Introduction, Methods, Results by tumor type and by mechanism, Discussion tying back to INRG). Methods are detailed enough to enable replication. Tables and figures are well-integrated. Minor issues include a few typos (e.g., 'phai29' for phi29), repetitive 'In conclusion' paragraphs, and occasional dense primer descriptions that might be better moved to the supplement, but overall clarity is good.

key_strengths: First systematic TMM analysis in a sizable GNB cohort (n=48) using a standardized C-circle assay
Multi-modal molecular characterization (C-circle, TERT mRNA/FISH/promoter sequencing, ATRX genomics, array CGH) with pre-specified cut-offs
Identification of ATRX alterations in 100% of ALT(+) GNBs and a recurrent 12.5 Mb 7q gain region in ALT(+) NTs
National cooperative group sampling with central pathology and molecular review
Direct relevance to potential INRG classification update and to ALT/TERT-targeted therapeutic trials
key_concerns: No clinical outcome/follow-up data linking TMM status to prognosis in the GNB and GN subgroups (authors acknowledge)
Small GN cohort (n=18) limits conclusions for that tumor type
TERT-high mechanism in GNB (no rearrangement or promoter mutation in most) is not resolved — only hypotheses advanced
Limited explicit data/code availability statement; CGH raw data do not appear deposited
REMARK checklist not explicitly invoked; some biomarker assay performance characteristics underreported
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid, methodologically rigorous biomarker study extending TMM analysis to GNB/GN with clear translational implications; fits a tier-2 specialty oncology or molecular-pathology journal after minor revisions to address outcome data limitations and reporting completeness.
